title: Brand cue by 5-7 s, inside action
statement: The brand appears as a cue inside the action by 5 s on paid YouTube, TikTok and paid in-feed ads, by 6 s on Reels and Shorts and by 7 s on X and LinkedIn, after the hook (>3 s) on organic feeds, and never as a logo card first.
evidence: Platform spec plus platform-commissioned studies: brand-lift began under 1 s in a feed study and brand cues in the first 2 s matched TV-level recall; a skippable-ad analysis found an early brand raised both recall and skipping.

sources.locator: 3.2 The hook (conflict to resolve by test); 8. Platform presets

notes: Conflict: TikTok-oriented agencies advise minimal branding in the first 5 s; the resolution is a diegetic cue (product in hand, the UI), pulsed in short repeated exposures (a study found pulsing reduced zapping vs one block). structures.json hook.brand_by_s (5, or 10 for saas-launch / founder-story) is not read by check_hook. | Merged: A brand cue lands inside the action (product in frame, UI, brand colour), never as a standalone logo card first, by 5 s on TikTok and paid YouTube or 9:16 feed ads, 6 s on Reels and Shorts, and 7 s on X and LinkedIn. [house; Platform spec for paid YouTube (brand inside 5 s); the organic values are pack defaults.] | templates/ad reports brandCueAt / brandCueOk but does not fail. patterns/hooks.json says 2-5 s for ads; formats.md says organic feeds tolerate the brand after the hook, before about 7 s; TikTok-oriented advice is minimal branding in the first 5 s. | Merged: The brand appears by 5 s on paid YouTube, Meta and TikTok, by 6 s on Reels and Shorts, and by 7 s on X and LinkedIn, after the hook. [house; paid YouTube 5 s from a platform ad guideline (second-hand) [S]; the organic values are a house resolution of a conflict [H].] | templates/ad/config.mjs computes plan.brandCueOk but nothing fails on it.

title: Flash-forward cold open for feeds
statement: A 9:16 feed cut of a slow film opens on a 1.5-2.5 s flash-forward of the conflict, then starts the story.
evidence: A turn arriving at 20 s in a vertical feed is listed as a recurring failure; the flash-forward is the craft fix.

title: Show visible motion by frame 6
statement: The first visible change happens by frame 6 (200 ms at 30 fps) and never later than 0.5 s, with at most one camera or layout move in the first 1.0 s.
evidence: House engineering default ([H]) built on practitioner agreement that the first 1-3 s decide the stay.
notes: The one-move limit in the first second is not checked. | Merged: Frame 0 is not black or near-uniform, and the first visible change lands by frame 6 (warn after, fail after 0.5 s). [house; pack hook rule; eyes found the shipped beat-edit template's first change on frame 11 and a demo with a black frame 0.] | visual.md: first text lands by frame 6-9. | Merged: Even a dark tease shows visible motion by frame 6 (<= 0.5 s), e.g. an edge light already moving on frame 0, never a still silhouette for 1 s. [measured; 19 Oct run: eyes/frame0 failed on 12 of 44 renders (7 templates); a device teaser showed nothing moving for its first 1.0 s.] | lint_shotlist also fails a black / fade-in frame 0 at script time. | Merged: Frame 0 is a strong image already in motion with its first visible change by frame 6 (<= 0.5 s); never black, never a logo bumper, never a fade-in; a small product-name super over moving footage inside 2 s is allowed. [craft; practitioner rule [P]; round 4/5: 0 of 29 references opened on a static logo and 7 of 29 (tier A among them) used a small name super over moving footage inside 2 s.] | Also failed by lint_shotlist (frame 0 black/logo/fade-in/title card) and structure_check.check_hook. One studied piece opening on 1.5 s of black had 910 views: an observation, not proof of cause.

title: First sound by frame 3
statement: The first audible event lands on frames 0-3, or the plan marks a quiet open of at most 2 s that ends on the first visual event.
evidence: House rule; platforms report sound-on dominance (YouTube 'almost entirely sound-on', platform-commissioned TikTok survey) without a timing number.

[measured; 13 of 28 round 4/5 references with audio open at least 6 dB under the body for 1-2 s while frame 0 moves, tier A among them; mixed tiers.] | Also ears/sync (audible event frames 0-3), ears/structure (planned open <= 2 s) and music/mixer.py lint R10, which waives frames 0-3 when plan.audio.quiet holds an open that ends on the first cue (+0.25 s).

title: Open frame 0 on the hook, moving
statement: Frame 0 is the hook image already in motion: never black, a logo, a title card, a slate, a bumper or a fade-in.
evidence: House rule consistent across platform guidance ('start big', message up front) and practitioner hook advice (remove logo bumpers and slow intros).

[house; patterns/hooks.json grades the universal frame-0 rule 'platform' (platform creative guides); the frame thresholds are pack defaults.] | lint_shotlist FAILs on a black/logo/fade-in/title-card first action; eyes/frame0 measures the first change on the MP4.

title: Frame 0 subject at 3:1
statement: Frame 0 holds one readable subject at >= 3:1 contrast against its surround.
evidence: A 16:9 feature-drop open measured 1.30:1 and failed eyes/frame0 (16-17 Oct and 19 Oct runs).
notes: Merged: At frame 0 the hero is the brightest or highest-contrast element, measuring at least 3:1 (WCAG ratio, 85th vs 15th luminance percentile around it); under 1.5:1 fails. [house; pack rule (one high-contrast hero, 3:1 for meaningful graphics) measured by eyes on decoded frame 0.] | frame-design also asks for at least one critically sharp edge on the hero in every still; that part is not measured.

title: Show hardware by 4 s
statement: A hardware launch shows the product within 0-4 s, unless a light reveal (an edge or band sweep from darkness, about +11 dB at 1 s) is itself the hook.
evidence: pattern across the hardware films of the 20-film launch study; one studied film hits +11.6 dB at 1 s on a light sweep.
notes: A teaser (6-15 s) deliberately never shows the product whole (RECIPE HW).

title: Show the stake, hold the twist
statement: Frame 0, the title and the first line show the stake but not the answer; the twist or result stays hidden through the first 1-3 s.
evidence: Hook rule from the story-script craft notes; no reach measurement attached.

sources.locator: Hooks: three variants on one body

notes: The payoff-first archetype deliberately shows the result on frame 0; use it when the end state itself is the hook, not when the story depends on the twist.

title: Break a cliche open inside 8 s
statement: An interrupted-cliche open plays the cliche for 1.5-8 s (default 3 s), stops it with a hard stop sound, a 300 ms freeze and the music cut on the stop frame, then hard-cuts to the real format already in motion.
evidence: A pattern seen across the pack's studied films (success-patterns, interrupted cliche), not tied to reach.

title: Never lead with an offer or deadline
statement: Use an offer only when it is real with honest terms, and never as the hook; discount and deadline framing showed no organic evidence.
evidence: round 4/5: offer-plus-deadline posts appeared only in tier-C or tier-B pieces; round 3: comment gates drove replies, not purchases.

sources.locator: 6. CTA and end; 9. CTA and end

notes: Merged: Do not use an offer, deadline or comment gate as the hook; use an offer only when real, with honest terms, after the product is shown. [measured; Offer-plus-deadline posts appear only in tier-C or tier-B round-4/5 pieces; a round-3 comment-gated launch with a celebrity gained 40% more views than its sibling but no more bookmarks.] | We do not claim the offer caused the low tier; it simply has no organic evidence.

title: Payoff-first: rewind by 1.2 s
statement: A payoff-first hook shows the finished result already moving on frame 0 (a slow push or reveal sweep), then rewinds or cuts to the start by about 1.2 s.
evidence: Practitioner archetype in patterns/hooks.json, graded 'practitioner'.
notes: templates/ad/config.mjs accepts hook.archetype 'payoff-first' (its default), but nothing sets or checks the 1.2 s rewind.

title: Real product on screen by 10 s
statement: A software launch shows the real product UI by about 10 s and its name by 15-30% of runtime; the studied films showed first UI at 0, 5, 12 and 16 s, and a feature drop shows the feature on frame 0.
evidence: Frame-sheet measurement of 4 studied software launch films (first UI 0-16 s), plus a practitioner teardown asking for the real product within about 10 s.

title: Build a small sentence word by word
statement: A sentence-led open builds small centred type word by word, at most 7 words at no more than 3.5 words/s, one word per half beat, holds the full line 2 beats, then cuts to the result on the next downbeat.
evidence: Seen in the 16 s problem section of a tier-A round-3 launch film (1.9x, 3.8% bookmarks), a saves-strong round-3 keynote breakdown and two craft-only concept films; the timing numbers are the part's defaults.

title: Social proof needs a real source
statement: A social-proof hook runs only with a measured number or a permitted quote whose source is on screen; a digit without a source fails.
evidence: patterns/hooks.json grades the archetype 'platform'; the sourcing requirement is a pack rule.

sources.locator: social-proof needs a claim with a source

title: Sound-on pill from 0.5 to 1.5 s
statement: On a muted-autoplay feed, a frosted 'sound on' pill shows as an outline on frame 0, is solid at 0.5 s and is gone by 1.5 s.
evidence: All 4 proof clips of a 1.8M-view launch thread use this exact timing (thread children, tier B by rule, read as C); the tier-A* hero gives the same cue as a title behind the subject at 1 s.
notes: One team's four clips: a default to tune, not proven by reach. The part's defaults already match (solidAt 0.5, outAt 1.5).

title: Presenter may speak on frame 0
statement: A founder-on-camera film may start mid-sentence on frame 0 with no quiet open (open within 1 dB of the body), the product UI resolving behind the speaker by 0.5 s and no logo or title until the last 2 s.
evidence: Round-8 film 02 (tier A, 5.5x followers, 82 s) speaks from 0.0 s at +0.2 dB against the body; the tier-A* launch hero (private study) also speaks on frame 0 with only the first 0.5 s 6 dB under the body.
notes: check_hook only enforces a sound on frames 0-3 (which this passes); it does not check that the sound is speech or that the logo is held back.

title: Hook text up by 0.3 s
statement: When the hook uses text it is on screen by 0.3 s (0.5 s on wide frames and voice-led explainers, tutorials and data stories) and is at most 7 words (4 for wordless spots, teasers and hardware films).
evidence: House default ([H]); platform guidance asks for the message up front and text overlays, without a timing number.

sources.locator: Cross-post patterns > Hooks in the first 2 s

notes: Resolved 21 Oct: 0.3 s (vertical) / 0.5 s (wide) stays the house target the checks use; tier-A launch films land readable text by 1.0 s, which passes as a WARN, not a FAIL. | Also eyes/readability (hook text by 0.3 s tall / 0.5 s wide, max 7 words) and lint_shotlist.hook_max_words. Hook text, VO and picture should say the same idea (layered hook, practitioner). | Merged: Hook text is on screen by 0.3 s (0.5 s on wide frames) with at most 7 words, and the poster frame carries at most 4 words. [house; house default [H]; platforms publish no hook thresholds.] | Also lint_shotlist.hook_max_words / poster_max_words and structure_check.check_hook. Launch beat sheets allow the claim by 2-3 s (L3) and a thesis sentence in 0-5 s (L1). Poster frame: one high-contrast subject readable at 120 px wide; title front-loads the payoff in about 50 characters (virality.md 6). | Merged: Hook text has at most 7 words and is on screen by 0.3 s in a vertical cut (0.5 s in a wide cut). [house; Pack defaults shared by the linter, the reading checks and patterns/hooks.json universal.hook_text.] | Merged: Readable on-screen text is on frame 0 or by 1.0 s, and in VO films the word lands with or before the first spoken word. [measured-A; 9 of 16 round-7 films show text by 1 s, including 3 of the 4 tier-A films (the fourth is a wordless music video); in every VO case the word arrives with or before the voice.] | The pack is stricter than the evidence: pattern hooks use text_by_s 0.3 and eyes/readability wants hook text by 0.3 s tall / 0.5 s wide.

title: Make three hook variants per body
statement: Every brief gets 3 hook variants with distinct archetypes on an identical body, so only the hook differs between them.
evidence: practitioner rule [P]; archetypes listed: payoff-first, pattern-break, claim-or-question, in-medias-res, curiosity-gap, social-proof, problem-agitate.

title: Title behind the subject at 1 s
statement: Over a held frontal portrait with a direct gaze, the first title word animates in behind the subject (the subject occludes it) at about 1.0 s.
evidence: The tier-A* hero of a 1.8M-view launch (distribution-assisted) does this at 1 s, reading as a sound-on cue; one film.
notes: n = 1; craft default, not a reach-proven rule.

title: Land the twist by 5 seconds
statement: On a short skit or story short, land the twist by about 5 s: half the viewers of every top Short were gone between 4 and 8 s.
evidence: own Shorts channel, 28 days, 1,002 views: every top Short lost half its viewers in 4-8 s; 83% swiped away.
notes: lint_shotlist.turn_window warns outside 0.30-0.80 of runtime (5 s of 15 s = 0.33 passes) but the absolute 5 s is not checked. Conflicts with the 15 s beat sheet in skills/story-script/SKILL.md (turn at 9-11 s).

title: Open on a short line, calm field
statement: In a type-led launch film, frame 0 shows 1-3 words (or a placeholder prompt) on a plain or gradient field, and the full hook line of at most 6 words reads by 1-2 s; no product shot first.
evidence: 3 of 3 tier-A video films in round 9 open on type or a prompt bar on a calm field (a category sentence; a call to a named audience; a placeholder prompt); the product world arrives at 2-4 s.
notes: eyes/readability enforces hook max 7 words and hook text by 0.3 s tall / 0.5 s wide; structure_check.check_hook adds text_by_s. Tiers were taken on posts 3.5-44 h old, two on the 1.5% bookmark knife edge; re-pull pending.

title: State the value inside 3 s
statement: The proposition lands in the first 3 s and the hook is complete by 6 s; a 15 s ad's hook ends by 2.5 s (17%) and a 30 s ad's by 3 s (10%).
evidence: Platform spec: a platform's ad guidance says proposition in 3 s, hook in 6 s, and its commissioned analysis credits 90% of ad-recall impact to the first 6 s (method not published).
notes: A view now counts on start, so judge a hook by 3 s hold and average view duration, not views.
